newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ MPs approve report on Peters, reject amendments.
newsitem.headline: NZ MPs approve report on Peters, reject amendments.

text.p: The 120-seat New Zealand Parliament on Thursday voted to approve a controversial report by its privileges committee into an alleged assault by Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on a backbench MP.
At the end of a two-and-a-half hour session, legislators carried a motion to accept the finding that Peters had not been guilty of a contempt of parliament's internal rules.
Amendments proposed by leaders of two opposition parties to reject the report's main conclusion and to refer the alleged assault to a higher legal authority were both rejected.
Peters declined to apologise for his conduct, as the committee had requested he do.
He was later quoted as telling Television New Zealand he would not be talking about the matter again.
